sections.content:
16,565 people

were counted on the census as "printers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Printers set up and operate various small offset printing presses and digital printing processes.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "printers" there were more men than women (84.5% compared with 15.5%).

This means "printers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 84.5% and women made up 15.5% of "printers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "printers" included:

  • security guards and related occupations
  • programmers and software development professionals
  • chartered surveyors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "printers", 17.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "printers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "printers" included:

  • finance officers
  • health and safety managers and officers
  • child and early years officers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "printers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "printers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "printers", 7.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.7% compared with 13.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (91.8%) than self-employed (8.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
